title: Sell Mineral Rights in Homestead, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Homestead, MT
metaDescription: Mineral owner near Homestead in Sheridan County, MT? A former engineer breaks down homestead-era severances and why this area sits on the Bakken's thin edge.
heroLead: The name Homestead is fitting, because most of the mineral title work I do in this corner of Sheridan County traces straight back to original homestead patents.
intro: Homestead is a small unincorporated community up near the Saskatchewan border, and like the rest of Sheridan County it's grain and cattle country first, oil country a distant second. Any real evaluation of what you own here starts with the county courthouse in Plentywood, not with a cold offer that skips the title work.

sections.heading: A Century of Chain of Title
paragraphs: Land in this part of Montana was largely settled under the Homestead Act and its later amendments in the early 1900s, and a lot of the original patents severed mineral rights out from the surface at some point over the following decades, sometimes at the time of patent, sometimes in a later sale. Tracing exactly when and how your family's interest was severed, and confirming the current recorded owner of record, is often more work than the value conversation itself, especially after three or four generations of inheritance and probate.

sections.heading: Where This Sits in the Bakken Story
paragraphs: Sheridan County is on the far western flank of the Bakken and Three Forks play, well outside the thicker pay zones that made counties farther east genuinely active. I've seen owners here get quoted numbers clearly benchmarked off Richland County activity, and it doesn't hold up once you look at actual well density and permitting near Homestead. If your tract has no history of drilling and no current lease activity nearby, that's the honest starting point for any conversation about value.

sections.heading: What a Fair Look Involves
paragraphs: I'd want to see your deed or division order, confirm the county's recorded ownership matches what you believe you hold, and check for any nearby permitting or leasing that would change the picture. For most owners out here, that review turns up a modest, undeveloped or lightly developed interest, and I'll tell you that directly rather than dress up a flank-county tract as core Bakken acreage.

faqs.question: How do I trace my mineral rights back to the original homestead patent near Homestead, MT?
faqs.answer: Start with the Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder in Plentywood. They hold the recorded chain of title, and in many cases the original federal patent record is also searchable through the Bureau of Land Management's General Land Office records online.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Homestead, MT?
faqs.answer: Not to any meaningful degree. This is the far western edge of the Bakken play, with thin pay and limited well density compared to the play's core in Richland County.

faqs.question: What documents do I need before getting an offer on my interest?
faqs.answer: A copy of your deed or the most recent division order if you're receiving royalty, plus any probate or inheritance documents if the interest passed through an estate. That's usually enough for a first honest read on what you actually hold.
